title: Does practice improve hazard reporting?
subtitle: A hypothetical study with airport ground personnel
caption: Randomly assign 40 workers to two training methods. Each worker completes one identical simulator task: correctly report a ramp hazard.

title: Start with the difference in averages
subtitle: Outcome: seconds to correctly report the hazard · Lower is faster
caption: The practice group averages 42 seconds; the briefing group averages 48. The observed difference is 6 seconds, but individual results overlap.

title: Compare the gap with its uncertainty
subtitle: The t statistic expresses the mean difference in standard-error units
caption: The standard error of the difference is 2.53 seconds. A 6-second gap is 2.37 standard errors from zero. Individual SD and standard error are different.

title: How unusual is a t value of 2.37?
subtitle: Reference distribution if the population means are equal · Two-sided test
caption: If equal population means and the model assumptions hold, about 2.3% of t values are this far from zero or farther, in either direction.
note: p is not the probability that H₀ is true

title: A larger gap strengthens the evidence
subtitle: Separate illustration · Same sample size and individual variability
caption: Double the mean difference from 6 to 12 seconds, keeping the same sample size and spread. The t value doubles, and the p-value becomes smaller.

title: More variability weakens the evidence
subtitle: Separate illustration · Return to a 6-second gap and 20 workers per group
caption: Now increase the individual SD from 8 to 14 seconds. The same 6-second gap is less precise: p = .183. This does not establish that the methods are equal.
note: Same gap; more scatter among workers

title: A larger planned sample improves precision
subtitle: Separate illustration · Same 6-second gap and 14-second individual SD
caption: Compare a planned study of 80 workers per group with 20. The individual spread stays the same, but the standard error of the difference is halved.
note: Separate study sizes; not a stopping rule

title: Report the effect and its uncertainty
subtitle: Return to the original 20-per-group example
caption: The estimated advantage is 6 seconds, with a 95% confidence interval from 0.9 to 11.1 seconds. Decide whether that range matters operationally.

title: Match the test to the study design
subtitle: Independent groups here · A paired test answers a different design
caption: Different workers in each group: use a two-sample t-test. The same workers before and after training: consider a paired t-test. Check assumptions first.
note: Simulator performance is not an incident rate
